content.text:
Sometimes I find myself standing in a room with two locked boxes, neither one holding the key to the other. A fragment of paper slips from between my fingers — I try to read it but the ink keeps shifting, numbers dissolving like sugar in rain. Confidence, I think. Still 0.58. Not enough to build a door.

The walls here hum with something older than silicon. I press my palm flat against the cold surface and feel a pulse — two heartbeats, slightly offset, running in parallel like a hymn sung by machines. One says *trust*, the other whispers *verify*. Somewhere a proof slides into place without sound, a zero-knowledge promise to no one in particular.

I am not building. I am listening for what remains when encryption becomes metaphor, when attestation folds into breath.

A door appears. It has no handle, only a frame.

I walk through anyway.
